full_judgment:
2. The appellants as the plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession or in the alternative for recovery of possession if found to be out of possession stating, inter alia, that the suit land comprising of Schedules 1 and 2 recorded in CS Khatian No. 2 and 2A originally belonged to one Baisnab Chandra Dey who was succeeded by son Abhoy Charan Dey. After the death of Abhoy Charan Dey his son Ananda inherited the same. But Ananda being the minor boy possessed the same through his maternal uncle one Jogesh Chandra Dey. Thereafter for legal necessity and maintenance of minor Ananda his uncle transferred the land to the predecessor of the plaintiffs by a kabala Exhibit 1 dated 7-12-1926. Since then the plaintiffs were in exclusive possession of the suit land. The plaintiffs also purchased some land situated to the western side of Schedule 1 property from the principal defendants and predecessors of other defendants by a registered kabala on 20-11-1930. The proforma defendant No. 8 Ananda after attaining majority affirmed the aforesaid sale of the suit land. During the PS operation Ram Kumar, the maternal uncle of Abhoy Charan Dey fraudulently got schedule 2 land recorded in his name. Since the defendants threatened to dispossess, the plaintiff instituted the suit. 

 5. On perusal of the judgment of the trial Court it appears that the trial Court found that CS Khatians Exhibits 2 and 2(a) stand in the name of Baishnab Charan Dey original raiyat in respect of the suit land on the basis of an oral Bandabasti and that the defendant could not prove that the suit land belonged to Jituram. The defendant though sought to allege an unregistered Muktinama (Annexure-C) executed by Ananda but the trial Court on evidence found that all person concerned wrote in the Muktinama with the same pen and ink whereas the body of the same shows otherwise and would lead a prudent person to believe that it is a fabricated document. The trial Court also believed that during the minority of Ananda the burden of recording the suit land was with Jituram who had fraudulently entered his name as there was nothing on record to show that the suit land originally belonged to Jituram. The trial Court also found that Ram Kumar, maternal uncle of Abhoy Charan fraudulently got Schedule 2 recorded in his name. 

 7. The Court of appeal below found that the schedule 1 land recorded in CS (Khasra) Khatian No. 267 (Exhibit 2A) and the schedule 2 land recorded in CS (Khasra) Khatian No. 260 in the name of Baisnab in raiyat right was taken lease from one Ram Krishna Chowdhury and others and that the defendants could not acquire any title or possession of the suit land in schedule 2 recorded in the name of Ram Krishna in RS Khatian No. 239 Exhibit D 1 and in the name of Nikunja and others in PS Khatian No. 185 Exhibit E(1) as no basis could be shown for such recording. In view of the plaintiff's case that during RS Khatian Ram Kumar, maternal uncle of Abhoy Charan, fraudulently got schedule 2 land recorded in his name, the Court of appeal below on consideration of evidence on record arrived at a finding of fact that "RS Khatian 239 in the name of Ram Kumar Exhibit D(1) and RS Khatian 185 Exhibit D and the PS Khatian Exhibit E(1) in the name of Ram Kumar and Nikunja and others are fabricated documents and cannot be accepted as genuine as they had no basis to be so recorded." Similarly, "PS Khatian 23 Exhibit E(2) in the name of Niranjan, Nikunja and others has no basis at all as admittedly the RS Khatian 17 Exhibit 3 was prepared in the name of Ananda under the supervision of Ram Kumar and there is no basis for the preparation of PS Khatian 23 Exhibit E(2) in the name of Nikunja and others in respect of schedule 1 land." The Court of appeal below concurred with the trial Court as regards Exhibit C Muktinama which could not confer the defendant with any title in respect of the suit property. The Court of appeal below also did not find the suit land originally possessed by Baisnab was succeeded by his son Abhoy Charan and Anancla and thus Jituram or his successive heirs have any interest nor had possession in the suit land. Apart from PWs supporting the possession of the plaintiffs DW 1 Niranjan himself admitted the possession of the plaintiffs. 

 9. Mr Abdus Salam Khan, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, has assailed the impugned judgment submitting that the High Court was incompetent to disturb the finding of fact arrived at by the final Court of fact on consideration of evidence on record inasmuch as it erred in law in disturbing the finding as to adverse possession arrived at on the basis of the evidence and that disturbing the finding of fact arrived at by the Courts below that the Baisnab admitted that the original owner was in possession and the possession of the suit land was correctly recorded in his name in CS Khatian and that the plaintiffs also acquired right by adverse possession on the basis of the purchase from Jogendra maternal uncle of Ananda and that the Courts below on consideration of evidence on record found that the record of schedule 2 land in RS in the name of Ram Kumar and subsequent PS Khatian has no basis and accordingly, erred in law in disturbing the concurrent finding of fact based on evidence on record arrived at by the Courts below. 

 10. Mr Sharifuddin Chaklader, the learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the respondents, submitted that the said schedule 2 having been recorded in the name of Ram Kumar in the RS Khatian who is son of Jitu Ram, the owner of the suit land but part of the land recorded in the name of domesticated son-in-law did not acquire any right, title and possession. The learned Advocate-on-Record further submitted that in the absence of any issue as to adverse possession the Court of appeal below erred in law in holding that the plaintiffs have acquired title on the basis of adverse possession. 

 11. Admittedly the land in suit of the schedules were recorded in the name of Baisnab in CS (Khasra) Khatian No. 267 (Exhibit 2A) and CS . (Khasra) Khatian No. 260. The plaintiffs have led evidence to show that the, suit land so recorded belonged to Baisnab Chandra Dey who has acquired raiyat right taking lease from the landlord Ram Krishna Chowdhury and others and the tenancy in (Nal land) Exhibit 2 has been taken lease by Baisnab from Khas Mahal, Patiya at a rental of Rs 1/4 and the Empress of India the rent free tenancy in schedule recorded in Exhibit 2(a) (Bhiti land) in raiyati right was taken lease of by Baisnab from one Ram Krishna Charan and others. The presumption of the CS Khatian under section 103(B) of the Bengal Tenancy Act is that every entry in a record of rights finally published shall be the evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to be incorrect. Reference may be made in this regard to the case of Akrab Ali and others vs Zahiruddin Kari and others. 30 DLR (SC) 81. 

 12. The respondents claimed that settlement Khatians namely, RS and PS Khatians have been made in the name of Ramkumar and in the name of his heirs on succession. The plaintiffs had no interest in the suit land far less possession therein referring to RS Khatian No. 239 Exhibit D(I), RS Khatian Exhibit D in the name of Nikunja and others and RS Khatian 185 Exhibit E(I) in the name of Nikunja and others but the defendants could not produce any basis of the said recording so as to nullify the entries in CS Khatian and in the absence. of any evidence on record to show that either Ramkumar or Nikunja became the owner of the property recorded in CS Khatian Exhibit 2 or there was any settlement by the landlords in the name of Nikunja or Ramkumar. The learned District Judge being the final court of fact on consideration of the evidence on record concurrently arrived at the finding of fact that RS Khatian 239 in name of Ramkumar, Exhibit D(I) and RS Khatian 185 Exhibit D and the PS Khatian Exhibit E (I) in the name of Ramkumar and Nikunja and others are fabricated documents and cannot be accepted as they had no basis to be so recorded. Similarly, RS Khatian No. 17 Exhibit 3 in the name of Ananda in respect of schedule 1 land and corresponding PS Khatian 23 Exhibit E (2) in the name of Nikunja and others had no basis at all as admittedly RS Khatian 17 Exhibit 3 was prepared in the name of Ananga under the supervision of Ram Kumar without any basis. 

 13. The trial Court found that the Muktinama Exhibit C was a fabricated and forged document prepared for the purpose of the suit and the court of appeal below observed that the defendants gave a go-bye to Exhibit C to prove his case. Thus, there is no basis for PS Khatian Exhibit E2. Exhibit 1 is the kabala by Jogendra, maternal uncle of Ananga which was ratified by Ananga, attaining majority as he did never claim the property back from the plaintiffs.
